### Farmer characteristics

[Final data: Farmer characteristics .](https://github.com/FoodSystemsModeling/CityFoodPolicy/tree/main/beef/data_final/farmer_characteristics.csv)

We use data from the restricted access 2022 Census of Agriculture to paramertize agents in the model. [Exported data](https://github.com/FoodSystemsModeling/CityFoodPolicy/blob/main/beef/data_processed/2026.07.15_NASS_export/CFP.beef_results_suppress.xlsx) and [code](https://github.com/FoodSystemsModeling/CityFoodPolicy/blob/main/beef/data_processed/2026.07.15_NASS_export/CFP.01.Beef_approved.qmd) used to generate results.

The sample of farms include farms in New York with primary commodity dairy and at least \$1,000 in sales. Another way to disaggreate data by scale is to use herd size, where operations with less than 300 dairy cows are small and 300 or more are large.

- For our sample of farms with gross cash farm income (GCFI) \<\$1M, the average dairy herd size is around 60.
- The correlation between the continuous variables GCFI and dairy herd size is 0.96.
- Almost all dairies with 300+ cows are on operations with GCFI \$1M plus. -- Of those farms with 10-300 cows, 15% are on farms with GCFI \$M plus and 75% are on farms with GCFI\<\$1M.

Due to the high correlation between GCFI under/over \$1M and herd size under/over 300, we use GCFI to indicate scale.

The sheet titled "summary" includes summary statistics (mean/standard error) for a variety of different farm-level characteristics by scale and MWBE.

The sheet titled "metadata" contains definitions of all variables and the sheet titled "info" describes the data at a high level along with the sample.

Notes: Operations with less than 1,000 in sales are dropped, if N\<5 it is not included, (D) indicated not included due to disclosure risk.

```{r}

# Import summary data
df <- read_xlsx("../data_processed/2026.07.15_NASS_export/CFP.beef_results_suppress.xlsx", 
                sheet="summary")

write_csv(df, "../data_final/farmer_characteristics.csv")

# Add meta data info
meta <- c(

  exp_cow = "Total expense per dairy cow",
  young = "An operation with a young operator (less than 35 years old)",
  beginning = "An operation with a beginning operator (10 years or less farming experience)",
  cropland_harvested_acres = "Harvested cropland acres",
  cropland_failed_acres = "Failed cropland acres",
  cropland_summer_fallow_acres = "Summer fallow acres",
  cropland_idle_acres = "Idle cropland acres",
  permanent_pasture_acres = "Permenant pasture acres",
  woodland_pasture_acres = "Woodland pasture acres",
  other_pasture_acres = "Other pasture acres",
  drained_tile_acres_pct = "Acres drained by tile as a percent of operated acres",
  drained_ditches_acres_pct = "Acres artifically drained by ditches as a percent of operated acres",
  conservation_easement_acres_pct = "Acres under conservation easement as a percent of operated acres",
  no_till_acres_pct = "Cropland acres where no-till practices used as a percent of operated acres",
```

## County data

[Final data: County- and state-level data on the number of dairy farms, dairy cow inventory, and number of organic dairy farms.  .](https://github.com/FoodSystemsModeling/CityFoodPolicy/tree/main/beef/data_final/county_dairy_farms_inventory.csv)

We download 2022 data from [U.S. Department of Agriculture, National Agricultural Statistics Service (USDA NASS), Data, Large Datasets](https://www.nass.usda.gov/datasets/).

We include data on the number of farms with at least 10 milk cows and milk cow inventory by county and total for the state. The restricted access data includes New York farms with primary commodity dairy and at least 1,000 in sales, N=2,163. This is very similar to the definition of a commercial dairy farm of 10 or more dairy cows (which we use in this section) where N=2,165.

However, milk cow inventory on farms with less than 10 dairy cows is not disclosed in some counties. All farms with inventory are counted, non-disclosed data is only for inventory of milk cows. Note this this is a slightly different definition that used in the restricted access data, but the two sample sizes are very closely alighned (no )

There are a total of 2,931 dairy cows not allocated across 7 counties due to disclosure. For commercial dairy farms (at least 10 dairy cows), this is 2,317. The number of commercial dairy farms in these 7 counties are mostly 0 or 1 (1 county has 2 and another has 5). This is less than 1% of milk cow inventory in the state.

We take the 2,317 milk cow inventory that was not disclosed and allocate it evenly across the counties with missing data based evenly split based on the number of commercial dairy farms.

#### Farms and inventory

```{r}

# Import county-level data for NY
coa <- read_tsv("../data_raw/qs.census2022.txt") %>% 
  clean_names()

# Keep NY only, state and county data 
df <- coa %>% 
  filter(state_alpha=="NY")

# Add fips
df <- df %>% 
  mutate(fips = case_when(
    agg_level_desc=="STATE" ~ state_fips_code, 
    agg_level_desc=="COUNTY" ~ str_c(state_fips_code, 
                                     county_code, sep = ""))
  )

# Make county name lowercase
df <- df %>% 
  mutate(
    county_name = str_to_title(county_name)
  )

# Convert value to numeric
df <- df %>% 
  mutate(value = as.numeric(str_remove_all(value, ",")))


# Keep data of interest
varlist <- c(
  "CATTLE, COWS, MILK - INVENTORY", 
  "CATTLE, COWS, MILK - OPERATIONS WITH INVENTORY"
)

df <- df %>% 
  filter(short_desc %in% varlist & 
           (domaincat_desc=="INVENTORY OF MILK COWS: (1 TO 9 HEAD)" | 
              domain_desc=="TOTAL")
  )

# Select columns of interest
df <- df %>% 
  select(fips, county_name, short_desc, domaincat_desc, value)

# Define farms/inventory
df <- df %>% 
  mutate(
    item = case_when(
      str_detect(short_desc, "WITH INVENTORY$") ~ "farms",
      TRUE ~ "inventory"), 
    type = case_when(
      domaincat_desc=="INVENTORY OF MILK COWS: (1 TO 9 HEAD)" ~ "less10", 
      TRUE ~ "all") 
  ) %>% 
  select(-short_desc, -domaincat_desc)

# Pivot wider to calculate inventory and farms for commercial dairy farms (at least 10 dairy cows)
df <- df %>% 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = c(type, item), 
    values_from = value
  )

df <- df %>% 
  mutate(
    commercial_dairy_farms = all_farms - 
      coalesce(less10_farms, 0),
    commercial_dairy_inventory = all_inventory - 
      coalesce(less10_inventory, 0)
  )
  
# Keep data of interest
df <- df %>% 
  rename(
    all_dairy_farms = all_farms, 
    all_dairy_inventory = all_inventory,
  ) %>%
  select(
    fips, county_name, all_dairy_farms, all_dairy_inventory, 
    commercial_dairy_farms, commercial_dairy_inventory
  )
```

#### Allocate missing

```{r}

# Missing
county_total <- df %>% 
  filter(fips != "36") %>%
  summarise(sum(commercial_dairy_inventory, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  pull()

state_total <- df %>% 
  filter(fips=="36") %>% 
  pull(commercial_dairy_inventory)

# Inventory to allocate across missing farms
diff <- state_total-county_total

# Number of farms to allocate across
missing_farms <- df %>%
  filter(is.na(commercial_dairy_inventory)) %>% 
  summarise(sum(commercial_dairy_farms)) %>% 
  pull()
  
# Per farm allocation
allocation <- diff/missing_farms

## Allocate based on number of missing
missing <- df %>% 
  filter(is.na(commercial_dairy_inventory)) %>% 
  mutate(
    commercial_dairy_inventory = round(commercial_dairy_farms*allocation)
  )

# Join with original data
df <- df %>% 
  filter(!is.na(commercial_dairy_inventory)) %>% 
  bind_rows(missing)

rm(missing)

# Keep only commercial dairy farm data
df <- df %>% 
  select(fips, county_name, commercial_dairy_farms,
         commercial_dairy_inventory)
```

#### Organic

We do not have data on the number of organic operations by county. We used the [USDA AMS database of certified organic farms](https://organic.ams.usda.gov/integrity/) and downloaded the New York data and filtered for dairies. We used ChatGPT to match the cities to counties and cross-checked it for accuracy with Claude. Using this data, we made a pivot table to quickly skim the top few counties for a manual check. We assume a county not listed has zero organic dairy farms. 

```{r}

# import data
organic <- read_csv("../data_processed/usda_ams_organic_farms_data/usda_ams_organic_dairy_counties_ny.csv") %>% 
  rename(
    county_name = county
  )

# get totals by county
organic_county <- organic %>% 
  group_by(county_name) %>% 
  summarise(
    organic_dairy_farms = sum(number_of_farms)
  )

# total by state
organic_state <- organic %>% 
  summarise(
    organic_dairy_farms = sum(number_of_farms)
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    county_name = NA
  )

organic <- bind_rows(organic_county, organic_state)
rm(organic_county, organic_state)

# Join organic to other data - fill NAs with 0
df <- df %>% 
  left_join(organic) %>% 
  mutate(
    organic_dairy_farms = case_when(
      is.na(organic_dairy_farms) ~ 0, 
      TRUE ~ organic_dairy_farms),
    fips = case_when(
      is.na(county_name) ~ "36", 
      TRUE ~ fips)
  )

```
Based on that, 90% of the dairy farms are in the following counties: 

```{r}
#| label: tbl-organic-dairy-counties
#| tbl-cap: "New York counties that account for 90% of certified organic dairy farms"

library(gt)

# import data
county_ranking <- read_xlsx("../data_processed/usda_ams_organic_farms_data/usda_ams_organic_dairy_counties_ny.xlsx", 
                            sheet = "County Ranking")

county_ranking %>%
  filter(!is.na(`Dairy Farms`), County != "Total") %>%
  filter(row_number() <= which(`Cumulative %` >= 0.90)[1]) %>%
  gt() %>%
  fmt_number(columns = `Dairy Farms`, decimals = 0) %>%
  fmt_percent(
    columns = c(`% of Total`, `Cumulative %`),
    decimals = 1
  ) %>%
  cols_align(align = "center", columns = Rank) %>%
  cols_label(
    `Dairy Farms` = "Dairy farms",
    `% of Total` = "% of total",
    `Cumulative %` = "Cumulative %"
  ) %>%
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = "USDA AMS Organic Integrity Database. Counties are listed through the first county at which the cumulative share reaches 90%."
  ) %>%
  opt_row_striping() %>%
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = px(14),
    data_row.padding = px(4),
    table.width = px(520)
  )
```
